title.narrative: Effective and inclusive labour market institutions that support the implementation of wage policies and the provision of employment services are reviewed, developed and strengthened

description.narrative:
Egypt has ratified in 1976 Convention 131 (Minimum Wage fixing convention), which promotes the adoption of a minimum wage system with a broad scope of application, taking into account both the needs of the workers and their family, and the economic factors. Previously, the country had also ratified convention 100 (Equal remuneration convention), calling for the equal remuneration for men and women workers for work of equal value. The realization of the principles laid down in these convention should also contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable development goals adopted by the UN general assembly of 2015, and more specifically the targets 8.5 (By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value) and 10.4 (Adopt policies, especially fiscal, wage and social protection policies, and progressively achieve greater equality). For the past 2 years, Egypt’s National Wages Council (NWC), headed by Minister of Planning and Economic Development, has been increasing the minimum wage for private sector workers taking into account the economic conditions of the establishments that are currently unable to comply, and their exception to that, starting from 1 January 2022.
Beyond statutory minimum wages, existing complementary mechanisms for the setting of adequate wages are weak, either at the national, sectoral or company level. A short study carried out by the ILO in 2018 revealed that the number of collective bargaining agreements registered by the Ministry of Manpower has been dwindling since 2011 (from 72 in 2011 to 29 in 2016). Moreover, the few existing agreements are mainly concern the company level. However, the enforcement of sound minimum wages -either statutory or negotiated- would be a timely support to the working conditions, in particular since the recent data highlights a context of lower wages and high gender pay gap.
